newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: ALPINE SKIING-VON GRUENIGEN TAKES SECOND SEASON WIN.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-VON GRUENIGEN TAKES SECOND SEASON WIN.

text.p: Switzerland's Michael Von Gruenigen scored a decisive victory in a men's giant slalom on Sunday, winning by a huge margin of 1.64 seconds for his second triumph of the season.
The 27-year-old Swiss, the giant slalom World Cup title holder, produced near-perfect runs in both legs on the demanding Podkoren piste for a winning aggregate time of two minutes 13.42 seconds.
Austria's Siegfried Voglreiter was a distant second in 2:15.06, his first-ever podium finish in a World Cup race.
Norway's Kjetil-Andre Aamodt, winner of the overall World Cup trophy in 1994, was third in 2:15.78. Both Voglreiter and Aamodt held their first leg places.
Alpine skiing's biggest drawcard, Alberto Tomba, disappointed the many Italian fans at the Slovenian resort by crashing out late on the second run.
Tomba, in his first giant slalom appearance of the season, was seventh after the first descent.
